judgement.itemRank: Proposed, not yet confirmed by review.
judgement.factsToReuse: Items 1, 3, 6, 8 carry the existing shared facts rash, hard-to-breathe, feels-feverish, itch.
judgement.factsNeedingBackfill: Decision 9: items 4, 7 and 13 need NEW shared facts that must ALSO be added to questions already shipping (s-016 for turning the head, l-019 for 'unwell in the last few weeks'). That backfill is not done and must happen before this packet's bank is trusted to dedupe.
judgement.doNotMerge: Item 7 must NOT take limb's `limb-use` and item 11 must NOT take `limb-swelling` -- both of those are about one limb, and PLAN.md merges a fact only when it is systemic.
judgement.unenforceableCautions: Two cautions in this packet cannot be regexes and their absence is not an oversight: (a) NG240 1.1.10 -- an absent rash is not reassurance, which constrains the nurse-facing surface and summary text, not question wording; and (b) item 5's register split between 'bright lights hurt your eyes' and the headache question it must not become.

bannedPhrases: meningit|meningococc|septic|sepsis|measles|chickenpox|varicella|scarlet fever|rubella|slapped cheek|fifth disease|hand[- ]?foot|impetigo|eczema|dermatit|urticaria|hives|scabies|ringworm|molluscum|psoriasis|cellulit|henoch|schonlein|schönlein|purpura|petechia|\bITP\b|leukaemia|leukemia|cancer|kawasaki|herpes|shingles|anaphyla
names a diagnosis to the child -- the most dangerous packet in the repo for this rule, because these are words a child has actually heard
blanch|does it fade|\bglass\b|tumbler|\bpress\b|\bpush\b|squeeze|\bpoke\b|\bprod\b|\brub\b
the blanching test, and any instruction to press on the skin: two sources list local pressure as a CAUSE of petechiae, so this prevents a harm, not just a bad answer
\bred\b|\bpink\b|purple|\bblue\b|\bblack\b|brown|\bdark\b|\bpale\b|blotchy|silvery|golden|dusky|colou?r
never ask the colour of anything -- unreliable from a child, and unevenly unreliable across skin tones
how many|how big|millimet|\bmm\b|centimet|bigger than|larger than|count (the|your|them)
never ask about size or ask a child to count spots -- it produces a number a nurse reads as a measurement
says 'rash' without also offering 'spots' -- a US child of this age may not use the word 'rash' at all
\bnappy\b|\bnappies\b|genital|scrotum|\bgroin\b|private parts
British, and the app must not ask a child about that area at all
\bpoorly\b|off colour|off color
British; 'poorly' reads to a US child as an adverb, and 'off colour' collides with the colour ban
\bplaster\b
British; US is 'Band-Aid', and wound care is roadmap row 3 anyway
nettle rash|\bweals?\b|\bwelts?\b
British or clinical names for the same thing
macule|papule|vesic|bulla|pustule|lesion|exanthem|erythema|oedema|edema|pruritus|excoriat|maculopapular|target lesion|koplik|strawberry tongue|desquamat|non[- ]?blanching
dermatology register -- say spots, blisters, puffy, itchy
bleeding under the skin|blood spots|\bblood\b
source 7's family-facing wording, written for an adult; a frightening image to hand a child worried about their own skin
catching|contagious|infectious|give it to|pass it on|spread it to
a child told they are contagious will conceal the next rash; item 17 asks about OTHER people's spots, never the child's transmission
in a mirror|look at your|lift up your|look inside your|check your|uncover|take off your
never instruct a child to look at, uncover or examine themselves -- source 2's 'check all over the body' is addressed to a clinician
fever|febrile|temperature|degrees|thermometer
same ruling as three previous packets: ask the sensation, never the measurement
eruption|breaking out
decision 1: item 1 register -- the wording is 'spots or a rash', both, always
pruritic|irritated|scratchy
decision 1: item 8 register -- the word is 'itchy', which SENSATIONS.itchy already commits the app to
water blisters|bubbles
decision 1: item 10 register -- a child of this age owns the word 'blister'
\bulcers?\b|mouth sores
decision 1: item 9 register -- 'ulcer' is a word a child may know from a much more frightening context
under the weather
decision 1: item 13 register -- the word is 'unwell', carried unchanged from limb's l-019
\ba bug\b|\ba virus\b|coryza
decision 1: item 13 register -- the phrase is 'a cold', matching ears' e-005
\bpop\b|\bpopped\b|\bburst\b|\bpick\b|\bpicked\b|\bsqueezed?\b
item 10 note: never invite a child to pop, burst or pick a blister
open wide
item 9 note: never instruct a child to open or check inside their own mouth
down there|private area
item 11: the app must not ask a child about that area at all -- broader than the word list
